Every 'golden' case is expected to FAIL RED against the current op-piet build (RED-baseline.txt records that state) and must turn GREEN once ivregress/reg3/reghdfe(2-way)/ivreghdfe land.
_meta.oracle_log: internal capture d1-oracle-stata.log (real StataBE 19.5, `import delimited piet/packaging/sample/fatalities.csv, clear`, 336 obs, sections D1a..D1i). d1x was upgraded from structural-only to numeric golden using the user-run StataNow professor-pangram log at pangram_stata_results.log (internal capture) (2026-08-01, 336 obs).
_meta.dataset_loader: sysuse fatalities, clear  (piet's own bundled-sample shortcut, ALREADY supported today — dispatcher.cpp `cmd=="sysuse"` arm, verified live against the fatalities.csv identical to the oracle's `import delimited` load: 336 obs, same columns). The driver prepends this line to every case's do_body — it is NOT part of a case's own do_body list.

tolerance_policy.rationale: Oracle values are STATA'S DISPLAYED coeftable/scalar numbers (default format), not e(b)/e(V) full float64 precision — each number's own true precision is bounded by its last displayed digit. Surveyed every pinned value across all D1a-i cases: worst-case coefficient/SE relative precision implied by display rounding is ~6.3e-4 (reg3 SURE emppop:income se = .0000799, 3 sig figs); worst-case scalar (chi2/F) relative precision is ~1.6e-3 (D1a chi2=3.05, 2 decimals). Tolerances below add a >1.5x safety margin over both, per Eval's own existing convention of 'display-precision tolerance, not full cross-impl float precision' (contrast tests/eval/piet2/tolerances.py's CROSS_IMPL table, which assumes BOTH sides have full float64 precision — not true here since one side is Stata's rounded display text).

coeftable_name_aliases.__note: PIET's existing feols coeftable rows use '(intercept)' (verified live, tests/eval/piet2/streams/debug_all.json block idx 134) while Stata's own display uses '_cons'. The D1 wiring may adopt either spelling for ivregress/reg3/reghdfe — the driver tries both before failing a coeftable lookup.

known_engine_gaps.iv-se-denominator: Operator gate feedback on the post-D1 build (2026-07-15): d1a-d coefficient cells PASS but their SE cells miss — a CHARACTERIZED engine gap, not a mystery RED. cobra's iv estimator uses an N-K small-sample denominator where Stata's ivregress defaults to asymptotic N; verified: sqrt(336/333)=1.0045 matches the got/want ratio exactly (e.g. 4274.77/4255.64 on d1c's beertax se). Engine fix queued for Phase F (cobra MINOR). Per Art 10 the tolerances and expected values stay EXACTLY as pinned — they are the Stata truth, and the affected cases MUST stay RED until the engine matches. Affected cases carry a per-case `known_engine_gap` key.

block_schema_expectation.single_equation: block['coeftable'] — list of {name,b,se,...} — plus top-level scalars (chi2, F, rmse, r2, adj_r2, r2_within, n_clusters, df1, df2), matching the EXISTING cobraToEstimation()/cobraToEstimationM4() passthrough whitelist (piet/native/src/handlers.cpp ~787, piet/native/src/estimation_m4.cpp ~167). Verified live against the current build's feols block (see tests/eval/piet2/streams/debug_all.json idx 134).
block_schema_expectation.multi_equation_reg3: block['outcomes'] — list of {depvar, coeftable, r2, r2_within, dof_resid}, matched by `depvar`. This is NOT a guess: piet/native/src/estimation_m4.cpp lines 140-165 (BS-065 comment) ALREADY documents that cobra's `reg3 --tidy` payload carries per-equation results under 'equations' ({depvar,coefs,coeftable}) and that estimation_m4.cpp's converter reuses the SAME 'outcomes' array shape other multi-model commands use, falling back to null for r2_within/dof_resid (reg3 doesn't emit those per-eq). The DISPATCH arm that recognizes Stata's `reg3 (...) (...)` syntax and calls this converter is what's still missing (the actual D1g/D1h gap) — the conversion plumbing is pre-existing. The driver also tries a flat 'equations' key and a colon-qualified flat coeftable ('depvar:varname') as fallbacks, in case the eventual wiring differs from this documented plan.
block_schema_expectation.ivreghdfe: The professor-pangram StataNow run supplies the previously missing numeric oracle. d1x now pins the endogenous-regressor coefficient and clustered small-sample SE instead of accepting any finite positive SE.

d1g_reg3_3sls.notes: 3SLS default (simultaneous system: emppop appears as a regressor in the income-side... actually income appears as regressor in the emppop equation, making income endogenous system-wide). chi2/rmse per equation are a SECONDARY check per _meta.block_schema_expectation (estimation_m4.cpp's current 'outcomes' remap does not carry per-eq chi2 at all — documented honest engine-data gap, BS-065 comment); if the eventual wiring also omits them, treat their absence as a schema note, not a numeric failure — only missing/mismatched coefs or r2 should fail the case.

do_body: reg3 (income beertax spirits) (emppop unemp income), sure
d1h_reg3_sure.notes: SURE (all-exogenous system, `sure` option) — different Sigma-weighting than 3SLS default, hence different b's/se's from D1g despite the identical equation specification. Confirms `sure` genuinely changes the estimator, not just a cosmetic flag.

d1i_reghdfe_cluster2way.stata: reghdfe income beertax, absorb(state) vce(cluster state year)
do_body: reghdfe income beertax, absorb(state) vce(cluster state year)
d1i_reghdfe_cluster2way.n_clusters_note: Stata reports 48 state-clusters AND 7 year-clusters for the ABSORB/cluster-count listing, but the SE-adjustment line ('Std. err. adjusted for 7 clusters in state year') uses 7 — the min(G_state, G_year) convention 2-way clustering's dof correction uses. Pin n_clusters==7 (the effective/reported adjustment count); if the eventual JSON instead exposes a list/dict of per-dim counts, that is a genuine schema question for the maintainer to resolve at wiring time, not a value this golden got wrong.
d1i_reghdfe_cluster2way.notes: THE defining test of this case is `se` under 2-way cluster(state year) — the point estimates (b) do not depend on vcov choice at all, so a wiring that silently only supports 1-way cluster (dropping to 1-way on `state` alone, i.e. ignoring `year`) would still get `b` right but MUST get `se` wrong versus these pinned values — that discrepancy is the actual signal 'reghdfe vce(cluster A B) 2-way' is really wired, not just parsed-and-ignored. Confirmed live (2026-07-15): reghdfe already dispatches today (aliased onto the same regress/feols path as 'regress'/'reg'/'feols' — piet/native/src/dispatcher.cpp ~1733) and absorb() already works; the gap is specifically that vce(cluster A B) with >1 cluster variable is NOT supported (piet/native/src/handlers.cpp ~841: 'twoway clustering is OUT of the M2 slice').

d1x_ivreghdfe_absorb.stata: ivreghdfe income emppop (beertax = spirits unemp), absorb(snum) cluster(snum)
do_body: ivreghdfe income emppop (beertax = spirits unemp), absorb(snum) cluster(snum)
d1x_ivreghdfe_absorb.notes: Upgraded on 2026-08-01 from structural-only to a real StataNow golden. The coefficient was already aligned; the defining pin is the cluster small-sample SE. The pre-fix PIET path omitted ivreghdfe's small-sample correction and returned 10003.01652769641, a 1.34% miss that this case rejects.

d1_boottest_engine_parity.oracle_section: NONE (by design — boottest is an SSC package, no Stata license entitlement gate here; see mission spec)
d1_boottest_engine_parity.stata_setup: regress income beertax spirits, vce(cluster state)
do_body: regress income beertax spirits, vce(cluster state)
d1_boottest_engine_parity.grading: Run the SAME do_body through piet_native TWICE (two separate --do invocations, cold session each time, identical fixed seed). PASS iff: (1) both runs succeed (rc==0, no stopped_at_reason) — two IDENTICAL failures are NOT a pass (there is no p-value to compare — 'engine-parity' can only be claimed for a real result); (2) every field in required_fields is PRESENT in both runs' boottest block (guards against a vacuous pass where parity_fields are all simply absent); (3) every field in parity_fields that is present in run 1's block is present and byte-identical (exact float equality, not tolerance — same seed through the same binary must reproduce bit-for-bit) in run 2's block; (4) a 'reps' field is present in the output and equals reps_requested (499) — proving reps was actually forwarded to the engine, not silently dropped.
d1_boottest_engine_parity.notes: Engine-parity-only per mission spec: no external Stata SSC boottest oracle is used. The wired implementation maps onto cobra's wild-cluster-bootstrap estimator (block estimator 'wild_cluster_bootstrap', fields p_symmetric/p_equaltail/seed/reps/t0/beta — coordinator-live-verified on the post-D1 build 2026-07-15). FIXTURE NOTE (operator gate feedback, 2026-07-15): the prerequisite fit MUST be a vce(cluster ...) regression — boottest is a WILD CLUSTER bootstrap and the wiring honest-rejects with 'boottest requires a preceding regression with vce(cluster ...)' after a plain-iid fit. The original authoring of this case used an unclustered `regress income beertax spirits` prerequisite, which kept the case RED on the post-D1 build for a FIXTURE reason, not a wiring reason; fixed to the clustered form.
